feed.title: Mobile Design Rounds
feed.subtitle: Mobile system design case studies for Android and iOS engineers

entry.title: Design a chat app
entry.summary: Outbox, safe retries (idempotent sends), and sync with WebSocket and push.

entry.title: Design a news feed
entry.summary: Paging, optimistic writes (show a change first), and keeping the cache fresh.

entry.title: Design photo backup and file sync
entry.summary: Uploads that can resume, sync by blocks, and edit conflicts.

entry.title: Design a pagination library
entry.summary: The library API, generic types, and which requests go first.

entry.title: Design an image loading library
entry.summary: Memory and disk caches, decoding, and cancelling requests.

entry.title: Design a hotel or ride booking app
entry.summary: Holds, server time, payments, and search.

entry.title: Design a stock ticker app
entry.summary: Streaming updates, limiting how often the screen changes, and an always-online app.

entry.title: Design a video streaming app
entry.summary: Loading ahead (prefetch), adaptive bitrate, and playback state.

entry.title: Design an analytics SDK
entry.summary: Sending events in batches, saving them on the device, privacy, and versions.

entry.title: Design a push notification SDK
entry.summary: How push tokens change over time, delivery, and deep links.

entry.title: Design a travel plans app
entry.summary: Friends edit a trip together, even offline, and no change is lost without a sign.

entry.title: Design a public transport app
entry.summary: A timetable that works offline, live delays on top, and careful use of location and battery.

entry.title: Staff-level mobile system design: what the round tests
entry.summary: How staff answers differ from senior answers, what interviewers can see, and a four-week practice plan.

entry.title: Offline-first mobile system design: one model, six case studies
entry.summary: The official offline-first model (the app keeps working without a network) used for chat, feed, upload, booking, analytics and push.

entry.title: Native vs cross-platform: write the decision record
entry.summary: A staff-level decision record (ADR) for choosing a framework. It covers criteria, the assumption that would change the choice, migration, parity tests, libraries with no owner, rollback, and a free template.
